name: ERPL
subtitle: Student-built liquid propulsion. From design to hot fire and flight.
description: The Experimental Rocket Propulsion Lab (ERPL) is a student-run engineering organization that designs, builds, and tests experimental rocket propulsion systems. Members gain hands-on experience across liquid propulsion, high-pressure fluid systems, avionics, structures, recovery, and flight systems. No prior experience is required to join.
philosophy: ERPL works in short design-test-analyze loops. Decisions stay close to the students doing the work; reviews, fault analysis, and procedural rehearsals exist to move good hardware safely toward test. Test data drives the next iteration across propulsion, fluids, electronics, and structures.
mission: ERPL exists to bridge the gap between classroom theory and real propulsion systems. Students graduate having designed hardware, executed test campaigns, and analyzed real engine data; experience rarely available at the undergraduate level.
whatsNext: ERPL is preparing MOE, its first flight-capable liquid bipropellant launch vehicle, for the Friends of Amateur Rocketry Dollar-Per-Foot Challenge on December 12, 2026.
